data.body:
## AC verification — all six confirmed INDIVIDUALLY against the landed source, then ticked

The previous session deliberately left the boxes unticked because ticking one asserts the item is
done and it had not checked each. I have now checked all six against the LANDED file
(`git show gerrit/main:tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py`,
521 lines, bb67d4f7f2), not against the agent's summary of it.

AC1 — CONFIRMED. `test_reader_recovers_every_seeded_issue_across_three_pages`, parametrized over
`sorted(_READERS)` = all three of get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map. Seeds 250
at page 100 (3 pages, so a fencepost cannot pass by accident) and asserts
`set(out) == {DIG-0..DIG-249}` — a SET comparison, not a `> 0` floor — plus payload identity at
indices 0, 105, 249 so a reader returning the right count of wrong items fails.

AC2 — CONFIRMED. `test_the_cursor_token_advances_across_requests` asserts on the recorded request
BODIES (`server.bodies`): request 0 must omit `nextPageToken`, request N must equal
`server.responses[N-1]["nextPageToken"]`, and all sent tokens must be distinct.

AC3 — CONFIRMED, and genuinely independent. `test_islast_alone_terminates_the_walk` has the final
page set `isLast: True` while STILL handing back a live token (asserted in the test setup itself),
so a token-only reader spins — isLast is isolated. `test_an_exhausted_cursor_alone_terminates_the_walk`
is parametrized `["absent-token", "null-token"]` with the final page carrying NO isLast (also
asserted), isolating the cursor condition in both spellings.

AC4 — CONFIRMED, with the variance stated plainly. `test_a_repeated_cursor_token_stops_the_walk_on_its_own`
asserts the CONTRACT (stop within two requests, and `not server.hard_stopped` so the harness's cap
did not do the stopping) under `xfail(strict=True)` citing [rebar:cabc-7a98-d173-4d7c]. The AC says
"it either raises or stops, and the test pins which"; today it does NEITHER, and that is what is
pinned — strict xfail means the current failure is recorded, not tolerated, and flips RED the moment
the guard lands. Production behaviour was out of scope for this test-parity ticket by its own
instruction, and the defect is filed. I am satisfied this meets the criterion's intent (the
behaviour is nailed down rather than left ambiguous) and am recording the wording variance rather
than papering over it.

AC5 — CONFIRMED. Seven mutations with per-mutation verdicts and verbatim failure messages are in the
mutation-ledger comment on this ticket, including the two that no other oracle catches (break on a
SHORT page -> only the short-page variant fails; drop either stop condition -> only the isolated
stop-condition oracles fail) and the vacuity mutation (glob drifted to `*.pyx`) which the guard test
itself survives, which is why the coverage teeth test exists.

AC6 — CONFIRMED. `test_no_cloud_whole_project_reader_skips_the_cursor_loop` AST-scans
`adapters/jira/*.py` (the file the guard reads is asserted to include `acli_graph.py`) for any
function POSTing `/rest/api/3/search/jql` without both a loop and a `nextPageToken` reference. It
shares its predicate with a teeth test that drives a synthetic offender and keeps a paginated reader
and a non-search POST as negative controls, and with a coverage test that fails if the scan ever
goes vacuous. DC's guard scans the DC transport only, so this closes the class on EITHER deployment.

INDEPENDENT EXECUTION CHECK: ran the landed module in this worktree —
**27 passed, 1 xfailed in 2.94s**, exactly the counts the implementing agent reported. The commit
bb67d4f7f2 is an ancestor of this worktree's HEAD, so the close's file_impact precheck reads real
history.

Closing `--class preexisting`: the coverage gap this ticket names predated the work and the work
filled it; no production behaviour changed (acli_graph.py unchanged at 606 lines).
